subtopics.title: Constitutional Status and Powers of the ECI
subtopics.summary: The Election Commission of India is a permanent, independent constitutional body under Articles 324 to 329 (Part XV), established in 1950. It administers elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, the President and the Vice President, and has been a three-member body since 1993. Its powers are administrative, advisory and quasi-judicial, and the Supreme Court in Mohinder Singh Gill (1977) treated the case as a cornerstone for its plenary powers.
facts: Permanent, all-India, quasi-judicial and independent constitutional body
Constitutional basis: Articles 324-329 (Part XV)
Ensures free and fair elections for Parliament, State Legislatures, President and Vice President
Three members since 1993: one CEC and two ECs
Administrative power: defining constituencies, preparing voter lists, scheduling elections
Advisory power: advises the President and Governors, guides during emergencies
Quasi-judicial power: resolves disputes over party recognition, allocates election symbols
Mohinder Singh Gill v. CEC (1977): cornerstone case on ECI's plenary powers under Article 324
Where laws are silent (Articles 327 and 328), ECI can act independently to safeguard free and fair elections
ECI can order a re-poll if the purity of the electoral process is compromised; judicial review usually comes after the election

subtopics.title: Appointment, Tenure and Removal of CEC and ECs
subtopics.summary: The CEC and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023 replaced the 1991 Act and provides for appointment by the President on the recommendation of a Selection Committee, following the Supreme Court's directive in Anoop Baranwal vs Union of India (2023). The CEC and ECs enjoy Supreme Court Judge-level salary and benefits. The CEC serves for six years or until 65 years of age, whichever is earlier, and is removed through the same process as a Supreme Court Judge.
facts: Anoop Baranwal vs Union of India (2023): five-judge bench directed appointment on the advice of a Selection Committee
Earlier, the President made appointments on the advice of the Prime Minister
The 2023 Act replaced the Election Commission Act of 1991 on conditions of service and transaction of business
Selection Committee: Prime Minister, a Union Cabinet Minister, and Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha
Search Committee, headed by the Minister of Law and Justice, proposes a panel of five names
Selection Committee can consider names beyond the shortlist and can function despite vacancies
Tenure: six years or 65 years of age, whichever is earlier; not eligible for re-appointment
An EC appointed as CEC: combined term as EC and CEC must not exceed six years
CEC and ECs enjoy Supreme Court Judge-level salary and benefits
CEC is removed by the same process as a Supreme Court Judge

subtopics.title: Electoral Rolls, SIR and the Right to Vote
subtopics.summary: An electoral roll is the official list of persons eligible to vote in a jurisdiction, and being listed on it is a legal prerequisite for casting a vote. Rolls can be revised intensively, summarily or in special cases. The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) is a focused, time-bound house-to-house verification by Booth Level Officers, and courts have held that deletion from rolls cannot rest on mere suspicion.
facts: Electoral roll: official list of individuals eligible to vote in a given election within a jurisdiction
Being on the electoral roll is a legal prerequisite for casting a vote in India
Publishing and updating rolls: ECI, state's Chief Electoral Officer, and state election commission
Article 325: no individual excluded from electoral rolls on grounds of religion, race, caste or sex
Intensive revision: complete fresh preparation of rolls through house-to-house enumeration
Summary revision: routine annual updating of existing rolls
SIR: house-to-house verification by BLOs to add missing voters, remove ineligible ones and correct entries
Lal Babu Hussein vs Electoral Registration Officer (1995): guidelines allowing deletion on mere suspicion struck down
Kuldip Nayar vs Union of India (2006): right to vote is statutory, not fundamental
Bihar SIR: those not in the 2003 rolls had to submit any of 11 listed documents to prove birth date or place

subtopics.title: EVM and VVPAT
subtopics.summary: The Electronic Voting Machine (EVM) records votes in place of ballot papers and boxes, and was first used in Paravur, Kerala, in 1982. The VVPAT prints a slip that lets voters verify their vote; the slip stays visible for seven seconds before dropping into a sealed box. In 2019 the Supreme Court ruled that VVPAT slips of five EVMs in every constituency should be counted instead of just one.
facts: EVM: electronic device used to record votes in place of ballot papers and boxes
First used in Paravur Assembly Constituency, Kerala, in 1982
Developed by Bharat Electronics Ltd (Bangalore) and Electronic Corporation of India Ltd (Hyderabad)
Two parts: Control Unit (with Polling Officer) and Balloting Unit (in voting booth)
VVPAT slip shows the serial number, candidate name and symbol
Slip is visible through a transparent window for 7 seconds, then is cut and falls into a sealed drop box
VVPAT machines can be accessed by Polling Officers only
VVPAT first introduced in the Noksen Assembly bye-election, Nagaland, in 2013
VVPAT used in all constituencies in the 2019 Lok Sabha elections
2019 Supreme Court ruling: VVPAT slips of 5 EVMs per constituency to be counted instead of 1

quizzes.title: CEC Appointment and Removal: MCQ Set
quizzes.passage: The Election Commission of India is a constitutional body, placed under Part XV of the Constitution, that administers elections to Parliament, the State Legislatures, and the offices of President and Vice President. Its job is to ensure free and fair elections across the country. Since 1993, it has functioned as a three-member body, with one Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and two Election Commissioners (ECs). Earlier, the President made these appointments on the advice of the Prime Minister. In Anoop Baranwal vs Union of India (2023), a five-judge bench directed that the CEC and ECs be appointed on the advice of a Selection Committee. Parliament then passed the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023 to comply with that directive. Under the Act, the Selection Committee consists of the Prime Minister, a Union Cabinet Minister and the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha. A Search Committee, headed by the Minister of Law and Justice, prepares a panel of names for the Selection Committee to consider. The Opposition has recently announced plans to move a motion in Parliament seeking the removal of the CEC. This has drawn fresh attention to the constitutional safeguards that govern the independence and removal of the CEC.

questions.q: National Voters' Day is celebrated on which date to mark the foundation of the Election Commission of India?
questions.explanation: National Voters' Day is celebrated on 25 January since 2011 to mark the ECI's foundation on 25 January 1950.

questions.q: The Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023 replaced which earlier Act?
options: Election Commission (Conditions of Service of Election Commissioners and Transaction of Business) Act, 1991
questions.explanation: The 2023 Act replaced the Election Commission (Conditions of Service of Election Commissioners and Transaction of Business) Act, 1991.

questions.q: Which case is regarded as a cornerstone in defining the plenary powers of the ECI under Article 324?
options: Mohinder Singh Gill v. Chief Election Commissioner (1977)
Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
S.R. Bommai v. Union of India
questions.explanation: The Mohinder Singh Gill judgment (1977) is described as a cornerstone for defining the ECI's plenary powers under Article 324.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Under Article 326, the right to vote is a fundamental right of every adult citizen.
Reason (R): In Kuldip Nayar vs Union of India (2006), the Supreme Court held that the right to vote is statutory, not fundamental.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Article 326 guarantees adult suffrage, not a fundamental right to vote, while Kuldip Nayar held the right to vote is statutory, so A is false and R is true.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Article 325   ->   A. Supervisory and controlling authority over elections and electoral rolls
II. Article 326   ->   B. Authority to act independently where laws are silent
III. Article 324   ->   C. No exclusion from electoral rolls on grounds of religion, race, caste or sex
IV. Articles 327 & 328   ->   D. Adult suffrage
questions.explanation: Article 325 bars exclusion from rolls, Article 326 guarantees adult suffrage, Article 324 gives supervisory authority, and Articles 327 and 328 let the ECI act where laws are silent.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the CEC and ECs:
I. The CEC and ECs enjoy salary and benefits equal to a Supreme Court Judge.
II. The CEC is eligible for re-appointment after completing a six-year term.
III. If an EC is appointed as CEC, the combined term as EC and CEC must not exceed six years.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement I and III are correct, while statement II is wrong because the CEC is not eligible for re-appointment.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about the appointment process are correct?
I. The Search Committee proposes a panel of five names.
II. The Selection Committee can consider names beyond the shortlist.
III. The Selection Committee cannot function while there are vacancies.
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are correct, and statement III is wrong because the Act allows the Selection Committee to function despite vacancies.

questions.q: Who was the first woman CEC, known for the shortest tenure of 16 days?
questions.explanation: V.S. Ramadevi was the first woman CEC and held the shortest tenure, of 16 days.

quizzes.title: Electoral Rolls and SIR: Typed Answer Set
quizzes.passage: An electoral roll is the official list of individuals eligible to vote in a given election within a specific jurisdiction, and being listed on it is a legal prerequisite for casting a vote in India. The publishing and updating of electoral rolls are the joint responsibility of the Election Commission of India, the state's Chief Electoral Officer and the state's election commission. The Commission has broad authority over voter list management, and no individual may be excluded from electoral rolls on grounds of religion, race, caste or sex. The Commission can direct a fresh revision of rolls, which may be intensive, summary or a combination of both. An intensive revision involves a complete and fresh preparation of rolls through house-to-house enumeration, and it is done when the rolls are outdated, inaccurate or need complete rebuilding. A summary revision is a routine annual updating of existing rolls, while a special revision is undertaken in exceptional cases. The Special Intensive Revision is a focused, time-bound house-to-house verification of voters by Booth Level Officers, aimed at adding missing voters, removing ineligible ones and correcting entries. Such a revision excludes non-citizens and includes citizens aged 18 or above who are ordinarily resident in the constituency. Courts have also held that names cannot be removed from voter lists merely on suspicion, and the right to vote is treated as a statutory right rather than a fundamental one.

questions.q: In which year did the earliest Special Intensive Revision listed in the booklet begin? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists SIRs beginning with 1952-56, followed by 1957, 1961 and later years.

questions.q: How many documents from the prescribed list can be submitted in the Bihar SIR to prove date or place of birth? (number)
questions.explanation: Voters not in the 2003 Bihar rolls had to submit any of 11 listed documents to prove date or place of birth.

questions.q: In which year was the last SIR held in Bihar? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the last SIR in Bihar was held in 2003.

questions.q: The 61st Amendment (1988) reduced the minimum voting age from how many years? (in years)
questions.explanation: The 61st Amendment lowered the voting age under Article 326 from 21 years to 18 years.

questions.q: Which 1995 case struck down ECI guidelines that allowed deletion from electoral rolls on mere suspicion? (name of the first party)
accept: Lal Babu Hussein vs Electoral Registration Officer
questions.explanation: Lal Babu Hussein vs Electoral Registration Officer (1995) struck down the guidelines allowing deletion on mere suspicion.

questions.q: Under which section of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 can the ECI direct a fresh revision of electoral rolls? (section number)
questions.explanation: Section 21(3) of the RPA, 1950 empowers the ECI to direct a fresh revision of electoral rolls.

questions.q: Under which Article does the ECI have supervisory and controlling authority over elections and electoral rolls? (article number)
questions.explanation: Article 324 gives the ECI supervisory and controlling authority over elections and electoral rolls.
